content: Metronidazole is a medication prescribed to treat acne rosacea, a chronic condition characterized by inflammation and sores on the facial skin. It helps reduce redness and the number of sores, although it may not completely cure the condition. Additionally, it is used to treat certain vaginal infections. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Metronidazole is available as a gel for topical application on the skin and as a gel for vaginal use. Typically, it is applied twice daily. For vaginal infections, it is used twice a day for five consecutive days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. When using metronidazole for acne, you may notice improvement in your symptoms within three weeks, with continued progress over the next six weeks or longer. It is important to continue using the medication as prescribed and not to stop without consulting your doctor, as discontinuing it may worsen your symptoms. Before applying the gel for acne, wash the affected area with mild soap and wait 15-20 minutes. Apply a thin layer of the gel and gently rub it into the skin. Avoid contact with your eyes. If your skin is dry, you may apply a moisturizer afterward, and you can use cosmetics, but consult your doctor for recommendations on suitable products. For vaginal use, the gel comes with a special applicator. Follow these steps for proper application: 1. Fill the applicator to the indicated level. 2. Lie on your back with your knees bent and spread apart. 3. Gently insert the applicator into your vagina and press the plunger to release the medication. 4. Remove the applicator and wash it with soap and warm water. 5. Wash your hands thoroughly to prevent spreading the infection. Apply the vaginal gel at bedtime, as the medication works best when you remain lying down after application. You may wear a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains, but do not use a tampon, as it will absorb the medication. Avoid douching during treatment, as it can wash out the medication and reduce its effectiveness. Continue using the gel even if you get your period during the treatment. Before using metronidazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs you are taking, especially anticoagulants like warfarin and any vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of central nervous system disease, liver or blood disorders, or Crohn's disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, discuss this with your doctor. If you become pregnant while using metronidazole, contact your doctor immediately. Do not consume alcohol while using the vaginal gel, as it may cause adverse reactions such as nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, headaches, sweating, and facial flushing. If you forget to apply a dose of the acne gel, do so as soon as you remember, but do not apply a double dose to compensate. For the vaginal gel, apply the missed dose the next morning or night and continue with your regular schedule. Metronidazole may cause side effects. Minor side effects include increased redness, dryness, burning, irritation, or stinging of the skin. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as stomach pain, fever, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge, require immediate medical attention. You or your doctor can report severe side effects to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store metronidazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Metronidazole is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Refrain from sexual intercourse during the five days of vaginal gel treatment. Do not share your medication with others. If your symptoms persist after completing the treatment, contact your doctor. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Metronidazole is available under the following brand names: MetroCream®, MetroGel®, MetroGel®-Vaginal, MetroLotion®, and Noritate®.
